newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian Deputy PM says political tensions eased.
newsitem.headline: Italian Deputy PM says political tensions eased.

text.p: Italian deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni said tensions between the centre-left coalition and hard-left allies, Communist Refoundation, had eased and that a deal on the forthcoming mini-budget would be found.
"The atmosphere is now more calm," Veltroni was quoted as saying by Ansa newsagency. "It is now clear that the (parliamentary) majority will not change," he added.

Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti on Thursday met Massimo D'Alema, the head of the largest coalition party, the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), to discuss the broad range of differences between the two sides -- including the planned mini-budget and privatisations.
"This (meeting) has set in motion a comprehensive solution to the problems," said Veltroni, the PDS's number two.
He added that as soon as the government knew how big the forthcoming mini-budget needed to be to meet the terms of the Maastricht Treaty, the government would reach an agreement with Refoundation.

The hard-left party holds the balance of power in the lower house of parliament and has strongly criticised government plans for fresh budget rigour as it seeks to become a founder member of European economic and monetary union (EMU). -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
